name: Kudzu Bug
symptoms: Clusters of small brown shield-shaped insects on stems and leaves Yellowing or browning of leaves Reduced plant growth and vigor Lower pod production in soybean Sticky honeydew deposits that may lead to sooty mold
description: A sap-sucking insect that attacks soybean and other legumes. Both adults and nymphs feed on plant sap, reducing plant growth and yield. Originally from Asia, it has become an important pest in several crop regions.
management: Monitor fields regularly for insect clusters Remove nearby kudzu plants when possible Use resistant or tolerant soybean varieties Encourage natural enemies in fields
prevention: Monitor fields early in the season Control kudzu near crop fields Maintain field sanitation and crop rotation
